subject.title: [Feature]: Allow writable custom binds with workspaceAccess: "none" for least-privilege sandbox access

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` allow normal file tools to write explicitly configured `docker.binds` targets whose resolved mount is `:rw`?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the choice changes sandbox host-write authorization and could conflict with the stricter fail-closed direction in the adjacent open PR, so automation should not choose the permanent security contract alone.

options.title: Approve Mount-Aware Writable Binds
options.body: Implement write authorization from resolved mount metadata so only explicit `:rw` bind targets are writable under `workspaceAccess: "none"`, with Docker/bridge/docs/tests proving `:ro` and workspace paths remain blocked.

options.title: Keep None Fully Non-Writable
options.body: Treat `workspaceAccess: "none"` as disabling all file-tool writes, close or reframe this request, and update docs so bind `:rw` does not imply normal file-tool writability in that mode.

options.title: Defer Into Broader None-Mode Policy
options.body: Resolve this together with isolated `/workspace` writability in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/37634 and the tool-surface gate in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/73385.

recommendation.title: Approve Mount-Aware Writable Binds
recommendation.body: Implement write authorization from resolved mount metadata so only explicit `:rw` bind targets are writable under `workspaceAccess: "none"`, with Docker/bridge/docs/tests proving `:ro` and workspace paths remain blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox bridge/mount/docs history and the security-boundary framing point most strongly to steipete for the product/security decision.
